topic: The Baghdad Battery — a 2,000-year-old clay jar that could make electricity

beats.narration: A 2,000-year-old clay jar that might have made electricity.
beats.image_prompt: ancient clay jar with copper cylinder inside, museum display lighting, dark background, mysterious archaeological artifact, highly detailed, no people

beats.narration: Found near Baghdad and dated to the Parthian or Sasanian period, it held a copper cylinder and an iron rod.
beats.image_prompt: cutaway illustration of an ancient clay vessel containing a copper tube and iron rod, technical archaeological style, warm lighting, no people

beats.narration: Filled with an acidic liquid, similar jars can produce a small voltage — enough for electroplating in modern tests.
beats.image_prompt: close-up of green copper corrosion and iron metal, scientific macro photography, dramatic side light, no people

beats.narration: Whether ancient people used it that way is still debated — no texts describe it as a battery.
